gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-sc: Wiry, upright and a bit mechanical: Nippo sets its lowercase nearly as tall as capitals, every stroke looking cut from wire. Noto Sans SC is the quiet one, with curves left open and short ascenders.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Tight wire and zero hairlines: Nippo's lowercase a is built from strokes that never thin out anywhere. Noto Sans Siddham works the other way, with a big central band and an s whose ends hang wide.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Noto Sans Sinhala lays down a dark, thick stripe of lowercase in every line, its curve endings keeping well apart. And Nippo above it holds a rope-like consistency through each stem, bowl and tail.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Nippo draws its line like spaghetti laid out in letters. Noto Sans Soyombo follows with a sizable x-height made for screens and curved letters with wide, unclosed mouths, so a long passage goes down smoothly.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Technical and contemporary, Nippo looks like pencil sketching where the pressure never changes, with small letters nearly capital height. Noto Sans Sundanese sits below with open-mouthed e crossbars.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Noto Sans Sunuwar is clean and approachable, with curves that leave daylight. Shrink Nippo and its rounded-wire strokes start to lose their presence, while enlarging the body would stretch those short ascender stems on tall lowercase bodies.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nagri: Nippo has a tube-like stroke that resembles neon glass, with lowercase standing nearly as tall as its capitals. Noto Sans Syloti Nagri brings short ascenders and a tall x-height beneath it.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Glass tubing over blown bulbs: Nippo keeps one unbroken line weight from terminals to junctions, which is its trick. Then Noto Sans Syriac takes over with tall rounded bowls and s shapes that turn wide and easy.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-syriac-eastern: Nippo looks like a bent-wire sign, constant in thickness and technical. Its best trait is the sharp divide from Noto Sans Syriac Eastern, whose tall lowercase towers over small caps and whose curve endings keep their distance.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-syriac-western: Cable-thick and wire-straight: Nippo's curves match its stems exactly, while Noto Sans Syriac Western holds its terminals far from the stroke body. That tension between tight and open is the pair's best quality.
